newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig to go it alone despite losses.
newsitem.headline: Grundig to go it alone despite losses.

text.p: Grundig AG, abandoned by its backer Philips N.V. due to massive losses, has decided to go it alone by slashing jobs and focusing on television manufacture, the company said on Thursday.
The supervisory board has approved a plan that would cut the workforce to 5,000 by the end of this year, 1,700 less than the current number and 3,600 less than at the end of 1996.

"Grundig wants to get slimmer and faster, to secure its future as an important player in the entertainment electronics field," supervisory board chairman Christian Schwarz-Schilling siad in a statement.
The company aims to break even by 1999, after losing 553 million marks ($328 million) last year and 598 million marks the year before, management board chairman Pieter de Jong said.
"We must learn again to believe in ourselves. We have the freedom to decide for ourselves," de Jong said.
The job cuts will concentrate on management levels. The plant in Nuremberg-Langwasser will not be closed, de Jong said.
After Philips' withdrawal, Grundig's capital has declined to 550 million marks. Philips will have to bear the 1996 loss, de Jong said, but he expects a legal battle.
He attributed the losses to price declines in Grundig's main markets and Philips management strategy, which favoured Dutch operations.
To survive, Grundig must reduce its loss to 100 million marks this year and 50 million marks next year. Initially, it had said it needed the cooperation of a strong international partner.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.686 German Marks)
